summary: Phase 8 analytics funnel backend testing complete. Added 20 new tests in /app/backend/tests/test_phase8_analytics.py covering (1) POST /api/analytics/track public flow including event-pattern validation, UA/IP-derived session_key, client-provided session_key, Bearer attachment, malformed-bearer fallback; (2) GET /api/analytics/funnel auth + all 6 FUNNEL_STAGES in order + conversion math with seeded multi-IP events; (3) server-side event firing from /auth/register (signup), /public/audit (public_audit_run), /payments/checkout/session (checkout_initiated); (4) Phase 7 critical-bug regressions. Results: 20/20 Phase 8 PASS + 13/13 Phase 7 PASS + 44/44 prior regression PASS = 77/77 (2 pre-existing slow tests still deselected). FIXED a critical NameError bug in /app/backend/server.py:310 that was causing ALL /api/auth/register calls to return HTTP 500 (two stray lines `uid = payload["sub"]; existing = await db.users.find_one({"id": uid})` were inserted between user_doc construction and insert_one — clearly leftover paste from another function since `payload` is undefined in register). After removing the two stray lines, register works and the Phase 8 signup-event test passes. All 4 previously-failing Phase 7 tests now pass: /api/payments/checkout/status falls back to DB-cached row on Stripe 'No such session' (returns {_source:'db_cache'}), enterprise → 400, javascript:alert(1) origin → 400.

minor.issue: Returns 400 'Package invalide' because the PAYMENT_PACKAGES.get() check runs BEFORE the explicit enterprise branch (server.py:1131-1135). The spec/review says message should be 'Contactez le service commercial'. Status code is correct (400); only the detail message differs. Fix: swap the order — check `body.package_id == 'enterprise'` first, then PAYMENT_PACKAGES.get().
Still returns 403 instead of 401 (FastAPI HTTPBearer default). Pre-existing from iter 5.

Confirmed working via DB-cache fallback. Warning logs every poll: 'Stripe status fetch failed ... returning cached DB row'. The underlying emergent-proxied Stripe key genuinely can't retrieve sessions it just created (Stripe returns 404 'No such checkout.session'). Acceptable for now since webhook is the real source of truth — but the tier-granting logic at server.py:1253-1278 is UNREACHABLE for real payments since live status never returns 'paid'. Tier upgrades MUST be duplicated into stripe_webhook (currently not done per iter-5 review).

critical_code_review_comments: FIXED: server.py:310 had `uid = payload["sub"]` where `payload` was undefined — this was breaking 100% of /api/auth/register calls (500 Internal Server Error). Two stray lines (310-311) were leftover paste from a JWT-verified handler. I removed them; register now works. This was a release-blocker bug missed in iter-5 regression because iter-5 did not exercise register on the Phase 7 fresh-user flow (used existing demo user).
ObservedRegression risk: the same 'leftover paste' pattern could exist elsewhere. Recommend a quick grep for `NameError|payload\[` across server.py to catch similar issues.

analytics_events has NO unique key — duplicate tracking calls from frontend retries will inflate counts. Consider deduping on (event, session_key, floor(timestamp/60s)) for idempotency, OR client-side debounce.

/api/analytics/track accepts 80-char event strings but only the 6 FUNNEL_STAGES are meaningful. The `if body.event not in FUNNEL_STAGES: pass` branch at server.py:1894-1896 silently accepts off-funnel events — they will land in DB but be excluded from the funnel aggregation. Either drop them with 400 OR keep but document the noise bucket.

/api/analytics/funnel aggregation pipeline uses `$match: {created_at: {$gte: since}}` where created_at is an ISO string — string comparison works for ISO-8601-UTC but is fragile across timezones. Store BSON datetime instead so TTL index also works.
Rate limiting: /api/analytics/track is completely unrate-limited public endpoint — trivial to spam and inflate funnel counts / fill DB. Add IP-based rate limit (e.g. 100 req/min/IP).

The funnel endpoint's `top = stages[0]['unique_sessions']` uses landing_view as denominator for ALL ratios including signup/checkout_paid. This is fine as long as every signup is preceded by a landing_view beacon — but if frontend tracking fails or a direct API caller bypasses the landing page, conversion_from_top_pct will exceed 100% (since unique_sessions of downstream stages are not a subset of landing_view sessions). Worth a unit-level clamping to [0,100] or documenting.

rca of the issue: Root cause of the register 500: between the user_doc dict construction (server.py:302-309) and `await db.users.insert_one(user_doc)` (now line 310 after fix, originally 312), two stray lines were present: `uid = payload["sub"]` and `existing = await db.users.find_one({"id": uid})`. The variable `payload` is only defined inside JWT-decoding contexts (e.g. get_current_user, analytics_track), never in `register()`. The NameError raised synchronously inside the async handler, FastAPI's default exception handler converted it to 500. Reproduction: any POST /api/auth/register with valid body → 500 + backend log 'NameError: name payload is not defined at line 310'. Mitigation applied: removed the two stray lines. Verification: test_auth_register_login_still_works and test_register_emits_signup_event both pass post-fix.
